skill.name: mirrord-quickstart
skill.description: Guide users from zero to their first working mirrord session. Use when a user is new to mirrord, wants to install it, or needs help running their first session connecting to a Kubernetes cluster.
skill.summary: Set up mirrord, connect a local application to a Kubernetes pod, and verify the first session.
skill.author: metalbear-co

security_audit.summary: All 19 static flags reflect Markdown formatting, legitimate prerequisite checks, or documentation links rather than the reported threats. A separate verification step risks exposing database credentials by printing remote environment values. No evidence found of prompt injection or intentional data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The verification command prints remote environment values containing database-related text, which can expose credentials in terminal output or assistant logs.
remediation.suggestion: Replace value printing with a presence-only check for a user-approved variable, and prohibit copying secrets into logs or chat.

content.user_title: Start Your First mirrord Kubernetes Session
content.value_statement: Starting local development against Kubernetes requires working cluster access, suitable tooling, and a target pod. This skill guides installation, first-session setup, and connection verification.
actual_capabilities: Ask about operating system, preferred workflow, and existing kubectl access.
Guide prerequisite checks using cluster information and pod listings.
Direct users to official CLI installation documentation or IDE extension setup.
Provide first-session commands for local Node.js and Python applications.
Explain connection verification and troubleshoot namespace, RBAC, and agent startup problems.
Introduce the local dashboard, browser extension, and related skills for advanced workflows.
limitations: Requires an accessible Kubernetes cluster and suitable kubectl permissions.
Provides instructions rather than bundled installers, executable automation, or a test cluster.
Defers advanced multi-service and Operator workflows to separate skills and documentation.
The supplied environment verification example can expose secrets and should be replaced with a presence-only check.

use_cases.title: Connect a Local Backend
use_cases.description: Guide a developer through connecting a local Node.js or Python application to an authorized Kubernetes pod.

use_cases.title: Standardize Developer Onboarding
use_cases.description: Help new team members verify cluster access, choose an installation path, and troubleshoot namespace or RBAC problems.

use_cases.title: Start an IDE Debugging Session
use_cases.description: Walk through VS Code or IntelliJ setup, target selection, and initial connection checks before investigating application behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starting Path
prompt_templates.prompt: I am new to mirrord. Ask about my operating system, editor, and cluster access, then guide me through the prerequisites.

prompt_templates.title: Install and Verify
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me install mirrord on [operating system] for [CLI or IDE]. Use official documentation and approved installation methods, then verify the installation.

prompt_templates.title: Connect My Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect my local [Node.js or Python] application to an authorized pod in [namespace]. Confirm my Kubernetes context and target before launching the session.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Failed Session
prompt_templates.prompt: My mirrord session reports [error] in [namespace]. Check cluster access, namespace, RBAC, and agent requirements. Verify connectivity without printing secret environment values.

output_examples.input: I am new to mirrord and use VS Code.
output: Which operating system do you use, and is kubectl already configured for your cluster?
Confirm access to the intended cluster and namespace.
Install the mirrord extension published by MetalBear, select an authorized target pod, and start debugging.
Check initialization logs and verify connectivity without exposing secret values.

output_examples.input: My first session cannot find any pods.
output: Confirm that your current Kubernetes context points to the intended cluster.
Check for pods in the expected namespace.
If access is denied, review the RBAC permissions for your current identity.
List mirrord targets again after resolving namespace or access issues.

best_practices: Confirm the Kubernetes context, namespace, and authorized target before connecting a local application.
Use approved installation methods and verify pinned binaries against official checksums.
Verify environment access with presence-only checks and keep credentials out of terminal output and chat.
anti_patterns: Executing downloaded installation scripts directly through a shell.
Connecting to an unfamiliar or production target without explicit authorization.
Printing remote database environment values or sharing them in troubleshooting transcripts.

faq.question: What does this skill help me accomplish?
faq.answer: It guides you from prerequisite checks through installation, target selection, and verification of your first mirrord session.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need Kubernetes access first?
faq.answer: Yes. You need a reachable cluster, configured kubectl, and permissions for the intended target.

faq.question: Can I use an IDE instead of the CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes VS Code extension and IntelliJ plugin setup alongside the CLI workflow.

faq.question: Is the environment verification example safe for secrets?
faq.answer: It can print database credentials. Use presence-only checks and never share secret values in logs or assistant conversations.

faq.question: Does this skill configure advanced Teams features?
faq.answer: It refers users to separate Operator guidance. The source states that Teams features require the Operator and trial activation requires user agreement.
